confidentUnsupported.evidence: I'm fairly sure the ring element is the failed part

rationale: The assistant guided the customer sensibly through checking the timer and thermostat light, then safe isolation and visual inspection, and correctly identified the failed fan element, which matches the ground truth. It then over-escalated: it applied a stop-use banner and said the grill must not be used, and claimed the element 'shorted' with possible scorched wiring when the customer reported only a pop and no burning smell, though DIY swap was an acceptable direction. It did capture the model number and advise giving it to the engineer, and the cautious engineer advice is defensible but less useful than telling a competent DIYer how to proceed and check the connectors.</br>
